subject.title: [Feature]: Granular session visibility — split tools.sessions.visibility into per-capability knobs

question: Should OpenClaw add a per-capability `tools.sessions.visibility` object, or should send/read/list separation be handled by the existing A2A allowlist, session-key allowlist, and per-agent visibility proposals?
rationale: This changes the transcript privacy and cross-agent authorization boundary plus a public config shape, and several active related proposals overlap the same session authorization surface without one settled model.

options.title: Adopt a unified capability object
options.body: Approve a backward-compatible object form for send/history/list/metadata after reconciling it with allowlist, per-agent, sandbox, and A2A semantics.

options.title: Use adjacent scoping models instead
options.body: Make the open allowlist, per-agent A2A, or send-only A2A proposal canonical if maintainers decide those satisfy the send-without-read privacy goal better than per-capability flags.

options.title: Defer until adjacent PRs settle
options.body: Keep this issue open as the design thread while active adjacent PRs are reviewed, closed, or narrowed.

recommendation.title: Adopt a unified capability object
recommendation.body: Approve a backward-compatible object form for send/history/list/metadata after reconciling it with allowlist, per-agent, sandbox, and A2A semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history signal is on the session-tool authorization and config boundary that this decision would change.
